subtitle: Lighter & HUD
- Game HUD on the Phone
- Lighter on Memory
- Easier on Battery
- Tiny Reconnects
---
**The shell's game HUD on the phone beside your keyboard**, and an app that weighs much less on the phone while it waits in the background.

### Game HUD
- **The Performance screen is now the shell's game overlay HUD**, so it can leave the game's screen: the frame rate big, with its average, 1% and 0.1% lows, the frame-time graph (spikes are stutters), the FPS cap and stutters; CPU with RAM, GPU with VRAM, the network and a laptop's battery; chips for the game, its resolution, the driver, the session time, the power profile and GameMode.
- **It follows the HUD you set on the PC** (*Settings → Game overlay → Performance*): the same rows, the bars or graph style, the accent, container or mono palette, the FPS target and the hot temperature.
- **Held sideways it fills the screen**, FPS, CPU and GPU side by side, with the system bars hidden; upright it is the HUD's column. One sample a second, only while the screen is open, and the PC samples only then.

### Lighter on memory and battery
- **The phone sleeps with its screen off:** workspaces, volume, toggles and PC copies no longer wake it; the latest of each arrives when the screen comes on. Calls, notifications, the PC's media and live activity still arrive at once.
- **Reconnects went from about 4.3 MB to about 14 KB:** the PC no longer sends its wallpaper again when the phone already has it.
- **About a third less memory in the background:** images and the GPU are only touched when a screen needs them, and the wallpaper behind the home card is let go when the app leaves the screen.
- **Fewer wake-ups:** no connection attempts over mobile data when the PC cannot be reached from there; the PC's media notification is posted only when what it shows changes; the media widgets let the launcher count their clock; the weather widgets share one alarm that does not wake the phone.

### PC wallpaper
- **Use the PC's wallpaper** now opens the phone's own wallpaper dialog (One UI's *Set as wallpaper*), so the system and other apps see the change; from the background a notification opens it.

**Needs the latest [ii-p3drovfx](https://github.com/P3DROVFX/ii-p3drovfx) shell (`dev` branch)** for the full HUD and the quiet link. With an older shell the Performance screen shows what that shell sends, and the link works as before.
